title: Quasi-ballistic ion transport boosts evaporation-driven electricity generation
abstract: Evaporation-driven electricity generation can utilize the abundant thermal energy in the atmosphere, but is limited by ion scattering in the energy-harvesting material. Machine learning has now enabled the design of vertical microrod generators that achieve quasi-ballistic ion transport, boosting the power density and power conversion efficiency.

title: Applying causal machine learning to assess and improve cleantech policy design
abstract: Effective clean technology (cleantech) policies, such as subsidies and carbon pricing, require an understanding of how interventions shape environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. To support targeted, evidence-based policy design, we discuss how causal machine learning can compare alternative policy scenarios and reveal where, how and for whom cleantech policies work.

title: A heat-driven route to elastocaloric cooling
abstract: A heat-driven elastocaloric cooling system is demonstrated in which two shape memory alloys perform complementary roles: one converts heat into mechanical work, while the other converts that work into cooling. This approach offers a pathway to electricity-minimized solid-state cooling using abundant low-grade heat sources.

title: A hidden leak in solids
abstract: Solid electrolytes have long been treated as materials that block electronic conduction while enabling fast lithium-ion transport. Two studies now show that residual electronic conductivity can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit, particularly in thin practical cells, and identify the limits needed to ensure long shelf life.

title: Integrated photovoltaics need design innovation and cross-sector collaboration
Lithium–disulfur dichloride batteries
abstract: Rechargeable lithium–sulfur batteries offer a promising route to high-energy storage using abundant sulfur, but their energy density is constrained by low operating voltage, sluggish redox kinetics and polysulfide shuttling. Raising sulfur to higher oxidation states could increase cell voltage, yet reversible high-valence sulfur chemistry in lithium batteries remains difficult because chloride species bind Li + and halogen-mediated reactions consume electrolyte. Here we show that a free-chloride-rich ionic liquid electrolyte enables a Li||S 2 Cl 2 chemistry that addresses these limitations by reversibly converting Li 2 S to S 2 Cl 2 through a three-electron sulfur redox process. The electrolyte functions as an ionic mediator with only a minor capacity contribution. This chemistry increases the average operating voltage from 2.05 to 2.54 V at 25 °C and 0.2C, raises sulfur-specific capacity by 58% and delivers an electrode-level specific energy above 1,700 Wh kg −1 with cycling over 100 cycles.

title: Halogen-assisted sulfur oxidation
abstract: Lithium-sulfur batteries have long been limited by lower operating voltage and shorter lifetime compared to traditional lithium-ion technologies. Now, system-level engineering enables the conversion of sulfur to disulfur dichloride, accessing the S+1 oxidation state, thereby delivering higher voltage and improved cycling stability.

title: Crystallization control of 2.0-eV bandgap perovskites for all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells
abstract: Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) perovskites are essential for monolithic all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells. However, their performance is limited by severe surface wrinkling, halide heterogeneity and large open-circuit voltage deficits originating from high Br–I ratios. Here we develop a surface reconstruction and halide homogenization strategy that simultaneously regulates crystallization and eliminates stress-induced morphological disorder in 2.0-eV bandgap perovskites. Through synergistic solvent and additive engineering, involving solvent-induced surface reconstruction and transient Cl − incorporation from oleylammonium chloride, surface wrinkling is suppressed, and Br/I crystallization is synchronized with promoted homogeneous halide distribution. The resulting UWBG perovskite films show uniform surface potential, suppressed non-radiative recombination, improved carrier mobility and an open-circuit voltage of 1.46 V. Integrating this UWBG subcell with optimized 1.6- and 1.22-eV absorbers yields monolithic all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells with 30.1% power conversion efficiency (certified 29.3%) and robust operational stability, providing a promising route towards >35% efficient all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics.

title: Ironing out the wrinkles
abstract: Ultrawide-bandgap perovskites are essential for all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells, yet their high bromide content causes surface wrinkling and halide disorder, limiting the performance. A surface reconstruction and halide homogenization strategy now enables a certified efficiency of 29.3% in all-perovskite triple-junction devices.

title: Smart energy must address enshittification risks
A unified distillation and electrolysis system
abstract: Seawater is an attractive feedstock for hydrogen production that overcomes community concerns about fresh water; however, electrolysis of seawater remains challenging. Now, a coupled alkaline water electrolysis and vacuum distillation in a unified process overcomes those challenges by using waste heat to treat seawater, enabling 250 kW-scale efficient co-production of hydrogen and fresh water.

title: A 250-kilowatt system for co-production of hydrogen and fresh water from seawater
abstract: Hydrogen production from seawater is attractive given its abundance, but direct seawater electrolysis is challenging due to the poor stability and low energy efficiency. ‌Here we report the co-production of hydrogen and fresh water from seawater by coupling alkaline water electrolysis with low-temperature desalination, wherein low-grade waste heat from the electrolyser drives seawater distillation to generate fresh water for both electrolysis and external use. A 20-kW industrial pilot system achieved co-productivities of 3.8 Nm 3 h −1 H 2 and 1.2 kg h −1 fresh water with stable operation for 100 days. Scaling up to 250 kW achieved 48 Nm 3 h −1 H 2 and 31.6 kg h −1 fresh water, with a 14.4% improvement in system electrical efficiency relative to alkaline electrolysis of fresh water alone. Techno-economic analysis of the coupled process indicates higher profitability than the traditional tandem process of desalination followed by electrolysis.

title: Exploring hydrogen pipeline costs by considering regional geographical and political characteristics
abstract: Transporting hydrogen using pipelines is becoming increasingly relevant in the energy system, yet current cost estimates typically rely on simplistic approaches that overlook region-specific characteristics, leading to potential miscalculation of costs. Here we examine hydrogen pipeline costs by incorporating regional geographical factors, such as land use, topography and existing infrastructure, together with political-economic factors represented through country-specific weighted average costs of capital. Using a geographic information system-based model, we demonstrate that the regional levelized cost of transportation can vary by up to a factor of three. Comparing our approach with conventional ones based on uniform detour factors in an existing European energy system analysis framework shows substantial deviations in trade flows and highlights the relevance of this work. We provide cost and route data for 4,900 potential global pipeline routes. Our findings yield insights for further research and stakeholders when assessing the economic viability of hydrogen as a competitive energy carrier.

title: Spatially informed policies can accelerate green hydrogen demand
abstract: Realized green hydrogen demand lags behind policy targets but could be accelerated by accounting for spatial spillovers, which refer to demand-side interdependencies where adoption by one user encourages further adoption by nearby users. Revising EU green hydrogen policies, including Hydrogen Valleys and European Hydrogen Bank auctions, to better account for these location-specific demand-side patterns could improve their effectiveness.

title: Spatially informed demand-side policies for green hydrogen diffusion in Europe
abstract: Green hydrogen faces an implementation gap: demand substantially lags policy ambitions. Here, combining an installation-level model of green hydrogen demand with an original database of >14,000 potential offtakers in Europe, we show that, conditional on diffusion patterns mirroring natural gas power generation (a historical analogue), demand-side spatial considerations are critical for closing this gap. Spatial spillovers—where local adoption increases adoption likelihood nearby—strongly shape diffusion, and their effect rises (>20-fold) when green hydrogen is not cost competitive. Spillover potential is concentrated in Central–Western Europe and hard-to-abate sectors: over half of the 10% most central installations are located in five German or Belgian industrial regions. Spatially informed policies deliver superior outcomes: targeting the most central offtakers improves policy cost-effectiveness by up to 41% (€0.96 kg −1 ) in a size, sector and cost-controlled setting and 15% (€0.20 kg −1 ) when following the European Hydrogen Bank auction format.

title: Rethink data centre planning
abstract: The rapid expansion of data centres is challenging power systems and planning processes to keep pace.

title: A Ni(OH)2 symmetric battery cell for hydroxide exchange membrane-based direct air capture of CO2
abstract: Electrochemical carbon capture is a promising low-energy-cost solution for direct air capture (DAC) by using renewable electricity and avoiding traditional, energy intensive thermal swing sorption. While several electrochemical devices have been proposed, few have achieved promised low energy costs while maintaining high durability and full purification of CO 2 ; moreover, scale-up and pressure drop are rarely considered for these devices. Here we show a symmetric nickel hydroxide battery design with a hydroxide exchange membrane durably tested in a laboratory-sized 25-cm 2 device for 5,000 h. Over a 48-h test, a scaled-up 9 × 300 cm 2 electrochemical stack achieved an energy cost of 132 kJ molCO 2 −1 and flux of 0.19 molCO 2 m −2 h −1 equivalent to 0.83 MWh tCO 2 −1 and 75 kgCO 2 m 2 yr −1 . In addition, the pilot-scale stack meets the 300 Pa pressure drop requirements for DAC. A pathway to below US$100 tCO 2 −1 is presented on the basis of energy technology learning rates, showcasing electrochemical DAC as a potential climate change solution.

title: From gigawatts to critical mineral demands for EU solar and wind
abstract: Decarbonizing the European Union’s energy system requires shifting from fossil fuels to material-intensive renewable infrastructure, yet the continental mineral demands of legally binding targets remain poorly quantified. Here we show that expanding solar, onshore and offshore wind capacity across the 27 member states through 2050 generates unprecedented demand for copper, zinc, silicon and rare earth elements, with supply-chain exposure highly dependent on the chosen technology pathway. Through three scenario-based projections, we find that pathways prioritizing offshore wind maintain rare earth element exposure near full-target levels (69.2 kilotonnes) even when solar and onshore deployment falls short, as these elements are technologically embedded in direct-driven turbine generators. These findings reframe the clean energy transition as a continental materials procurement challenge where mineral security functions as a binding feasibility constraint. Delivering climate goals requires institutionalizing material stress tests in national deployment plans, establishing strategic component reserves and actively securing international midstream processing partnerships.

title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture
abstract: Achieving energy-efficient carbon capture with membranes requires materials that combine high gas permeability and selectivity, long-term stability and scalable solution processability. Conventional mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) cannot fully exploit the intrinsic transport properties of porous filler because high filler loadings often lead to aggregation and non-ideal interfacial effects. Here using a weak-interaction inlaying strategy that overturns the conventional reliance on strong polymer–filler interactions, we report all-organic MMMs that embed single-crystal covalent organic frameworks (COFs) within a continuous polymer matrix. By balancing polymer–filler and filler–filler interaction energies, our approach enables high COF loadings of up to 75.5 vol% while maintaining uniform dispersion and excellent interfacial compatibility. The resulting membranes preserve the intrinsic structure and transport properties of single-crystal COFs, creating filler-dominated pathways for fast CO 2 transport. Consequently, they achieve CO 2 permeability of 74,800 Barrer while maintaining a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of ~20. Besides, the MMMs based on polyimide can retain ~85% of the initial permeability after 6 months of ageing at room temperature.

title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
abstract: Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization.

title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
abstract: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
abstract: Interventions to address energy poverty have expanded following the 2021–2023 energy crisis, but evidence on their effectiveness for improving health and living conditions remains limited. Here we use data from WELLBASED, a European study exploring the impact of interventions for energy poverty and improving health in six European cities. By categorizing interventions into structural, small measures, advice and financial support, we differentiate between the energy poverty and health impacts of each category. Through longitudinal analysis, we find there is little, if any, effect from small home improvements and energy advice, but that structural interventions for energy poverty have some positive thermal comfort and health effects. Direct financial support has clear positive effects on health and energy-saving practices, and when financial support fluctuates, so do participants’ living conditions. Governments should invest in a range of measures, with a recognition that structural measures and consistent financial support are most effective.

title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
abstract: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising route to high area-normalized power output. Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers reduces reliance on bromide, largely mitigating light-induced halide segregation and shifting the dominant stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers. Here we identify perovskite lattice compliance, the ability of the crystal lattice to elastically accommodate stress, as a materials descriptor governing photothermal stability. Across the compositions studied, higher lattice compliance promotes photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain accumulation, shifting deep-level defects towards shallower states and reducing band-edge energetic disorder. Guided by this absorber-level design principle, bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems achieved a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm −2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination and retained 90% of their initial efficiency after over 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun at 65 °C). These results establish lattice compliance as a physically testable framework for designing stable perovskite absorbers.

title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
abstract: Solution processing has great advantages in lowering the cost for fabricating chalcopyrite solar cells, yet challenges remain in controlling the crystallization process and achieving desirable composition. Here we show a precursor linkage strategy to achieve uniform Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 chalcopyrite thin films using simple metal salts and thiourea (Tu) as precursors. By introducing an acetate anion (OAc − ) with both hydrogen- and coordination-bonding capabilities, a molecular network connecting Cu–Tu and In– or Ga– complexes can be established in the precursor solution, which facilitates controlled reactions and prevents the formation of undesired secondary phases during crystallization. The coordination between Ga and OAc − also enables uniform and complete Ga alloying for high-purity single-phase Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 films. The resulting solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53% (certified 17.53%). Our work shows that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved by rational and precise design of solution chemistry.

title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
abstract: Electric power systems are evolving into cyber–physical infrastructures shaped by power electronics and digital control. As inverter-based generation alters system dynamics and digitalization heightens vulnerability to errors and attacks, cyber–physical coupling can also introduce subtle system-level effects. Here we show that grid-frequency time series worldwide exhibit a persistent 1-min oscillatory pattern whose origin has remained unexplained. We show that clock-synchronized control software in digitally controlled energy devices, particularly uninterruptible power supplies and battery energy storage systems, generates periodic power-demand peaks that propagate across voltage levels and can give rise to the observed pattern. The pattern amplitude has increased substantially in several grids over recent years, contributing to wear and tear in hydropower systems and motivating stricter frequency-control requirements. The rapid expansion of battery storage, data centres and the Internet-of-Things may further amplify such cyber–physical power oscillations, highlighting the need for improved control design.

title: Durable reactive CO2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts
abstract: Electrochemical carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction using low-carbon electricity provides a means to decarbonize chemical and fuel production. However, CO 2 reduction typically requires high-purity CO 2 obtained through capture and subsequent energy-intensive regeneration. Reactive capture integrates CO 2 capture and conversion, avoiding the desorption step, but existing systems show poor durability. Here we show that the pH swing intrinsic to reactive-capture systems drives protons towards the cathode, creating an acidic microenvironment that accelerates catalyst demetallation. To address this, we construct a covalently linked cobalt (Co) phthalocyanine catalyst supported on carbon nanotubes, in which early ~50% Co leaching generates vacancies and induces cooperative contraction of neighbouring Co sites, strengthening Co–N coordination and suppressing further demetallation. The resulting self-reinforcing vacancy–network interaction enables continuous operation for over 1,000 h at 50 mA cm −2 with ~80% carbon monoxide Faradaic efficiency and 39% energy efficiency at 2.9 V. These findings provide a pathway towards robust molecular catalysts for reactive carbon capture and electrochemical conversion.

title: Ironing out oxygen instability
abstract: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.

title: An extra beat every minute
abstract: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.

title: Caloric cooling devices and systems
abstract: Caloric cooling technologies, including magnetocaloric, elastocaloric, electrocaloric and barocaloric effects, are emerging as solid-state alternatives to conventional refrigeration, with the potential to eliminate high-global-warming-potential refrigerants. However, translating these material-level effects into efficient and scalable cooling systems remains a major challenge. Here we review the development of caloric cooling devices and systems, focusing on performance, scalability and prospects for practical deployment. We benchmark key performance metrics, including efficiency, temperature span, cooling power density, durability and cost, against vapour-compression and thermoelectric technologies. Despite large caloric effects, a gap persists between intrinsic material performance and device-level operation. Recent advances, including fatigue-resistant shape memory alloys, multilayer electrocaloric architectures and natural rubber-based elastocaloric systems, have improved durability, power density and cost-effectiveness. We further analyse system integration and cost trends and outline a roadmap to accelerate the transition towards sustainable cooling technologies.

title: Directing solvent reactivity
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) offer a promising route to low cost, high-energy-density energy storage, but their practical application is limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here we report a molecular-level electrolyte design strategy that mitigates sodium loss by simultaneously promoting highly reversible sodium deposition and suppressing electrolyte decomposition, enabled by the cyclic ether 1,3-dioxane (DOX). Weak coordination of DOX with Na + facilitates Na + desolvation and reversible sodium deposition, while controlled DOX oligomerization forms a thin and robust solid–electrolyte interphase that suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition and stabilizes sodium plating/stripping. As a result, 300-mAh-level AFSB pouch cells with a cathode loading of ~20 mg cm −2 retain ~80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C, operate at rates up to 3 C, maintain 88% capacity at −40 °C and achieve a round-trip energy efficiency up to ~98%. These results demonstrate a molecular electrolyte design strategy for extending the lifetime of AFSBs.

title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI 3 , is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. Here we identify that sparse doping of oversized FA cations induces severe grain boundary (GB) distortion, thereby facilitating defect generation and performance deterioration. To mitigate this, we develop a Pb-based metallomesogen that forms a mesophase exhibiting both solid-like and liquid-like properties. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI 3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI 3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing.
